newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines looking to buy more wheat - traders.
newsitem.headline: Philippines looking to buy more wheat - traders.

text.p: Philippine wheat importers are expected to scout for more bargains next week while feed millers are seen retreating to the sidelines after buying 150,000 tonnes of U.S. corn, grain traders said on Friday.
"For the U.S. wheat market, we will buy if prices fall to interesting levels," said one executive in a local flour mill.
"We are also looking at very interesting offers from Argentina and Australia," the executive added.
One firm recently bought 7,500 tonnes of western white wheat for November shipment, Manila dealers said, adding that they had received inquiries for an additional 25,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
Traders also said another Philippine flour mill is in the market for 15,000 tonnes of Australian soft wheat, to make cakes, pastries and noodles, for December shipment.
"More and more Philippine firms are getting interested in Australian wheat, which have competitive rates to U.S. wheat," another trader said.
The prevailing retail prices of flour in Manila remained unchanged at 290 pesos per 25 kg for hard flour and 260 pesos for soft flour, the Trade and Industry Department said.
Corn buyers, on the other hand, are waiting for official approval to import an additional 250,000 tonnes of corn to fill-up the expected shortfall from now up to the first quarter of 1997.

"The Department of Agriculture has asked the Bureau of Agricultural Statistics to come up with data to determine projections by livestock farmers of a corn shortfall up to the first quarter of 1997," deputy administrator Eduardo Gomez of
the state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) told Reuters.
The NFA bought 150,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn No 2 on Tuesday at an average price of US$161.10 a tonne C&F.

Traders said the prevailing retail price of yellow whole grain corn for feeds increased to 7.20 pesos from 7.0 pesos per kg while the retail price of white whole grain corn for starch edged up to 7.40 pesos from 7.30 pesos per kg.
